bahir vṛttiṃ hātuṃ citibhuvam udārāṃ nivasituṃ yadā bhāvābhedaṃ prathayasi vinaṣṭormicapalaḥ | sthiter nāśaṃ devī kalayati tadā sā tava vibho sthiteḥ sāṃsārikyāḥ kalayatu vināśaṃ mama sadā
sa: bahir vṛttiṃ hātuṃ citibhuvam udārāṃ nivasituṃ yadā bhāvābhedaṃ prathayasi vinaṣṭormicapalaḥ | sthiter nāśaṃ devī kalayati tadā sā tava vibho sthiteḥ sāṃsārikyāḥ kalayatu vināśaṃ mama sadā

en:
kram-p17 (17)
jagatsaṃhāreṇa praśamayitukāmaḥ svarabhasāt svaśaṅkātaṅkākhyaṃ vidhim atha niṣedhaṃ prathayasi | yamaṃ sṛṣṭvetthaṃ tvaṃ punar api ca śaṅkāṃ vidalayan mahādevī seyaṃ mama bhavabhayaṃ saṃdalayatām
sa: jagatsaṃhāreṇa praśamayitukāmaḥ svarabhasāt svaśaṅkātaṅkākhyaṃ vidhim atha niṣedhaṃ prathayasi | yamaṃ sṛṣṭvetthaṃ tvaṃ punar api ca śaṅkāṃ vidalayan mahādevī seyaṃ mama bhavabhayaṃ saṃdalayatām

en:
kram-p20 (20)
taditthaṃ te tisro nijavibhavavisphāraṇavaśād avāptāḥ ṣaṭcakrakramakṛtapadaṃ śaktaya imāḥ | kramād unmeṣeṇa pravidadhati citrāṃ bhavadaśām imābhyo devībhyaḥ pravaṇahṛdayaḥ syāṃ gatabhayaḥ
sa: taditthaṃ te tisro nijavibhavavisphāraṇavaśād avāptāḥ ṣaṭcakrakramakṛtapadaṃ śaktaya imāḥ | kramād unmeṣeṇa pravidadhati citrāṃ bhavadaśām imābhyo devībhyaḥ pravaṇahṛdayaḥ syāṃ gatabhayaḥ

en:
kram-p23 (23)
samagrām akṣālīṃ kramavirahitā sātmani muhur niveśyānantāntarbahalitamahāraśminivahā | parā divyānandaṃ kalayitum udārādaravatī prasannā me bhūyāt hṛdayapadavīṃ bhūṣayatu ca
sa: samagrām akṣālīṃ kramavirahitā sātmani muhur niveśyānantāntarbahalitamahāraśminivahā | parā divyānandaṃ kalayitum udārādaravatī prasannā me bhūyāt hṛdayapadavīṃ bhūṣayatu ca

en:
kram-p25 (25)
prakāśākhyā saṃvit kramavirahitā śūnyapadato bahirlīnātyantam prasarati samācchādakatayā | tato 'py antaḥsāre galitarabhasād akramatayā mahākālī seyaṃ mama kalayatāṃ kālam akhilam
sa: prakāśākhyā saṃvit kramavirahitā śūnyapadato bahirlīnātyantam prasarati samācchādakatayā | tato 'py antaḥsāre galitarabhasād akramatayā mahākālī seyaṃ mama kalayatāṃ kālam akhilam

en:
kram-p28 (28)
itthaṃ svaśaktikiraṇaughanutiprabandhān ākarṇya deva yadi me vrajasi prasādam | tenāśu sarvajanatāṃ nijaśāsanāṃśusaṃśāntitākhilatamaḥpaṭalāṃ vidheyāḥ
sa: itthaṃ svaśaktikiraṇaughanutiprabandhān ākarṇya deva yadi me vrajasi prasādam | tenāśu sarvajanatāṃ nijaśāsanāṃśusaṃśāntitākhilatamaḥpaṭalāṃ vidheyāḥ

en:
Whatever I have truly done, O Lord — no duty of mine goes beyond this: my pride has been offered by me with devotion on the Lord's lotus feet. This is my all; I know there is nothing other than this. Therefore, having cast all else aside — quickly, O protector of the helpless, O ocean of compassion — be pleased!
yatsatyaṃ tu mayā kṛtaṃ mama vibho kṛtyaṃ tu nātaḥ paraṃ yanmanmānamaiśapādakamale bhaktyā mayaivārpitam | sarvasvamata evametaditarannāsyeva jānāmyatastyaktvā kṣipramanāthanātha karuṇās
sa: yatsatyaṃ tu mayā kṛtaṃ mama vibho kṛtyaṃ tu nātaḥ paraṃ yanmanmānamaiśapādakamale bhaktyā mayaivārpitam | sarvasvamata evametaditarannāsyeva jānāmyatastyaktvā kṣipramanāthanātha karuṇāsindho prasanno bhava

en:
O Maheśa, at Your door let this charming speech of mine flash forth exceedingly — "Victory, victory to Maheśa!" — faultless and unceasing. Let this very speech, auspicious, be bliss-giving for me forever. O Lord, O giver of refuge, make me — whose protector is Maheśa — possessed of a protector!
maheśa tvaddvāri sphuratu rucirā vāgatitarāṃ mamaiṣā nirdoṣaṃ jaya jaya maheśeti satatam | śivā saiṣā vāṇī bhavatu śivadā mahyamaniśaṃ maheśanāthaṃ māṃ śaraṇada sanāthaṃ kuru vibho
sa: maheśa tvaddvāri sphuratu rucirā vāgatitarāṃ mamaiṣā nirdoṣaṃ jaya jaya maheśeti satatam | śivā saiṣā vāṇī bhavatu śivadā mahyamaniśaṃ maheśanāthaṃ māṃ śaraṇada sanāthaṃ kuru vibho

en:
You speak not, O best-limbed one; You look not upon me, wretched as I am. My entreaty, made in many ways, You hear not; You come not into my mind. Fallen amid the pit of the ocean of transmigration, I am mostly left unsupported — yet scripture truly declares You devoid of speech, sight, hearing, feet and the like!
brūṣe nottamāṅga paśyasi na māmetādṛśaṃ duḥkhitaṃ vijñaptiṃ bahudhā kṛtāṃ na śṛṇuṣe nāyāsi manmānase | saṃsārārṇavagartamadhyapatitaṃ prāyeṇa nālambase vākcakṣuḥśravaṇāṅghriṇādirahitaṃ
sa: brūṣe nottamāṅga paśyasi na māmetādṛśaṃ duḥkhitaṃ vijñaptiṃ bahudhā kṛtāṃ na śṛṇuṣe nāyāsi manmānase | saṃsārārṇavagartamadhyapatitaṃ prāyeṇa nālambase vākcakṣuḥśravaṇāṅghriṇādirahitaṃ tvāmāha satyaṃ śrutiḥ

en:
From the guru's word — by the force that wipes away the fabric of heaped-up reasonings — and from the assurance told, fittingly, out of regard for scripture: when the cloud of doubt has dissolved, let me touch the feet of the Lord, whose splendor shines in the sky of the heart — like the sun, the conqueror of darkness.
gurorvākyādyukti-pracaya-racana-unmārjana-vaśātsamāśvāsācchāstraṃ prati samucitādapi kathitam | vilīne śaṅkābhre hṛdayagaganodbhāsimahasaḥ prabhoḥ sūryasyeva spṛśatu caraṇān dhvān
sa: gurorvākyādyukti-pracaya-racana-unmārjana-vaśātsamāśvāsācchāstraṃ prati samucitādapi kathitam | vilīne śaṅkābhre hṛdayagaganodbhāsimahasaḥ prabhoḥ sūryasyeva spṛśatu caraṇān dhvāntajayinaḥ

en: Much time dwelling with You has passed — alas, in this very moment! What, what has not been done by You for me, for the sake of serving the excellent guru! Again and again I, whose body has attained the incomparable divine plane — yet indeed I forget You. Therefore, by You let there be no further staying-away! *Fidelity: preserved (all 5 verses, full pāda coverage from T1). Added: connective phrasing only. Not resolved: the formation prāsuvatkāyaḥ (v. 5c) is obscure; glossed as "whose body has a
sa: yātastvatsahavāsato bahutaraḥ kālo vatāsmin kṣaṇe kiṃ kiṃ vā na kṛtaṃ tvayā varagurūpāsānimittena me | vāraṃ vāramahaṃ punarnirupamāṃ divyaṃ bhuvaṃ prāsuvatkāyastvāṃ kila vismarāmi yadataḥ stheyaṃ na bhūyastvayā

en:
Distinct from the illumination of sun, moon, lamp and the rest, it does not shine — on account of over-pervasion; and hence: of the nature of light, just this much — illumined-illuminator named is mere convention.
arkendudīpādyavabhāsabhinnaṃ nābhātyativyāptatayā tataśca | prakāśarūpaṃ tadiyatprakāśyaprakāśatākhyā vyavahāra eva
sa: arkendudīpādyavabhāsabhinnaṃ nābhātyativyāptatayā tataśca | prakāśarūpaṃ tadiyatprakāśyaprakāśatākhyā vyavahāra eva

en:
No thing at all is dually distinct from knowledge; made of this and that, in consciousness there is no difference. From self-luminosity, hundredfold, in the one abode — the individual would not indeed be divided.
jñānadvibhinno na hi kaścidarthaḥ tattatkṛtaḥ saṃvidi nāsti bhedaḥ | svayamprakāśācchatam aikadhāmni prātisvikī nāpi vibheditā syāt
sa: jñānadvibhinno na hi kaścidarthaḥ tattatkṛtaḥ saṃvidi nāsti bhedaḥ | svayamprakāśācchatam aikadhāmni prātisvikī nāpi vibheditā syāt

en:
Thus — dense own-consciousness, one indeed: he is Śiva, the universe's supreme light. There too, indeed, shines, in variegated power: apprehended-apprehender-division-difference.
itthaṃ svasaṃvidghana eka eva śivaḥ sa viśvasya paraḥ prakāśaḥ | tatrāpi bhātyeva vicitraśaktau grāhyagṛhītṛpravibhāgabhedaḥ
sa: itthaṃ svasaṃvidghana eka eva śivaḥ sa viśvasya paraḥ prakāśaḥ | tatrāpi bhātyeva vicitraśaktau grāhyagṛhītṛpravibhāgabhedaḥ

en:
That difference, and this — not different thence: of the free, most-perfectly-clear one-abode. Palace, elephant, horse, cloud, ocean, mountain and the rest — just as of jewel-mirror and the like.
bhedaḥ sa cāyaṃ na tato vibhinnaḥ svacchandasusvacchatamaikadhāmnaḥ | prāsādahastyaśvapayodasindhugiryādi yadvanmaṇidarpaṇādeḥ
sa: bhedaḥ sa cāyaṃ na tato vibhinnaḥ svacchandasusvacchatamaikadhāmnaḥ | prāsādahastyaśvapayodasindhugiryādi yadvanmaṇidarpaṇādeḥ

en:
If, in a mirror's belly, the reflection-making with-prototype would be mind-proven — then in the interior of the mirror of free consciousness, among things there is no other cause besides.
ādarśakukṣau pratibimbakāri sabimbakaṃ syād yadi mānasiddham | svacchandasaṃvinmukhuraantarāle bhāveṣu hetvantaram asti nānyat
sa: ādarśakukṣau pratibimbakāri sabimbakaṃ syād yadi mānasiddham | svacchandasaṃvinmukhuraantarāle bhāveṣu hetvantaram asti nānyat

en:
O consciousness-dense one — therefore you indeed are supreme; in you indeed the universes shine at once. And they flash forth by the power of your glory; you indeed are also their supreme-Lord maker.
saṃvidghanas tena parastvam eva tvayyeva viśvāni cakāsati drāk | sphuranti ca tvanmahasaḥ prabhāvāt tvam eva caiṣāṃ parameśakartā
sa: saṃvidghanas tena parastvam eva tvayyeva viśvāni cakāsati drāk | sphuranti ca tvanmahasaḥ prabhāvāt tvam eva caiṣāṃ parameśakartā

en:
Thus — self-consciousness, primordially established, unaccomplishable; the self, non-lord, lord; whose place and time are full of own power — eternal, pervasive: Bhairava-Lord, I praise.
itthaṃ svasaṃvedanam ādisiddham asādhyam ātmānam anīśam īśam | svaśaktisaṃpūrṇavadeśakālaṃ nityaṃ vibhuṃ bhairavanātham īḍe
sa: itthaṃ svasaṃvedanam ādisiddham asādhyam ātmānam anīśam īśam | svaśaktisaṃpūrṇavadeśakālaṃ nityaṃ vibhuṃ bhairavanātham īḍe

en: This septad of good conduct — dissolved other thoughts — those desiring the ultimate rightly remember in the heart. Those, O Bhairava's one, again enter the supreme abode, and know the ultimate-thing-discussion of the three worlds. *Fidelity: preserved (all 8 verses, full pādas from T1). Added: connective phrasing only. Not-resolved: jñānadvibhinna read as dually distinct; śatam kept as printed (hundredfold) against tempting satatam; mukhura read as mukura (mirror); vadeśakālam obscure, glossed
sa: sadvṛttasaptakam idaṃ galitānyacintāḥ samyak smaranti hṛdaye paramārthakāmāḥ | te bhairavīya paradhāma muhur viśanti jānanti ca trijagatīparamārthacarcām

en: Of one who neither meditates nor chants, manifestation may come without any preparatory rule. Just so — O light of Śiva — we bow to him who possesses devotion.
My self stays young, drinking the nectar of Your devotion — though greyed as if with the dust of worldly journeying and its passions.
For those who have gained that wealth — the possessors of devotion dwelling in Your city — even movement along worldly paths happens by that very expansion.
Lord — where the whole world within worlds directly consists of You, what is not the devotee's field, and whose mantra does not succeed?
Victory to those intoxicated with the finest wine of devotion's nectar-essence! Though non-dual, they are ever Your second, O Lord.
Lord of the ocean of endless bliss — only they know Your truth who are densely drenched in blissful devotion's nectar.
You alone, Lord of the self, are the nature of all, and all loves dwelling in the self. Knowing Your devotion as self-established (*svabhāvasiddhā*) — by immersion's means — may a person conquer.
Lord — when the knowable is destroyed, by whom are You not seen, standing alone? Even amid the agitation of knower and knowable, You are easily seen by devotees.
As the lake of endless bliss, the Goddess, the beloved, is inseparable from You — so may one devotion of mine be inseparable.
O All-pervading — for devotees of devotion, everything is a cause of gaining You. This path of consciousness stands threefold — in joy, in suffering, in delusion.
What of knowledge — even its supreme state, from tasting Your devotion's nectar — is to me, O husband-Lord, like vinegar-sourness after wine.
Those to whom the great knowledge of Your devotion has come through practice — they alone know truth, both knowledge and its absence.
From the root, this creeper of speech, unfolding in due sequence — watered by the nectar of Your devotion, may it bear rasa-rich fruit for me.
"Having become Śiva, let him worship" — so the devotee is said to have become. For You alone are the body's essence, purified by devotees through non-duality.
For devotees, what is not a means to accomplishment of non-duality with You? And for the low, what obstructions could there be to its failure?
That You are attained sometime, somewhere, by yoga, O Lord — that is the deceit. Otherwise, how would You shine in all states for the possessors of devotion?
Untouched by withdrawal and the rest — this is the great distinction: that sharers of devotion stay composed even in emergence, beyond the yogins.
No yoga is enjoined, no austerity, no procedure of worship at all. On this guileless path of Śiva, devotion alone is praised.
My covering shattered by devotion's light shining from all sides — may even my thoughts, which face all real things, perish.
A wonder: that in devotees, with the single word "Śiva" standing always on the tongue's tip, there is the taste of every sense-object.
In the calm-waved, cool, clear, sweet milk-ocean of devotion's nectar — in tasting its unworldly essence — who that stands firm there is counted low?
Why would people like me not chew Your devotion's great medicine — whose after-taste, O Lord, is called liberation?
Those alone are ultimately wealth, O Lord, in the judgement of the good — which nourish confident enjoyment of the taste of devotion to You.
They have grasped something of Your devotion-nectar's essence who, though fallen into this mud of passion and the rest, are not smeared by it.
From supernormal powers to liberation — "fruit" is named as a mere limb of the ripened creeper of Your devotion, for some.
A wonder, Lord: this mind, by nature pain's seed — watered by the essence of devotion to You, becomes liberation's great fruit.
To the many-formed, whose nature is consciousness — fire, moon, sun, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, moving and unmoving — bow.
To the great fire fed by the universe as fuel, smeared-pure with great ash, to the Becoming to whom the world is the sole oblation — bow.
To Śiva-fire — cool, dense with supreme nectar — and to You, the unequalled devourer in the world's destruction — bow.
To Mahādeva, to Rudra, to Śaṅkara, to Śiva, to You Maheśvara — and to someone mantra-bodied — bow.
To Śiva-fire — cut, dried up, the three worlds' melted fat the oblation — unequalled, yet auspicious — bow.
To the god — to gracious someone — for whom the meeting of all marks is itself the mark — bow.
To the hidden Lord — Veda-opposing, Veda-making, the Veda's true essence, secret master — bow.
Sole cause of the wheel of births and deaths — and its sole opponent; saṃsāra-formed, saṃsāra-free — to gracious Śambhu, bow.
To root, to middle, to tip; embodied as root-middle-tip; with tip-middle-root exhausted — to the Full, gracious Śambhu — bow.
Even once — whosever taking of the Name — ripened heaps of merit. To You, Śiva, hard to attain — bow.
To You alone — consciousness-formed, skull-bearing — ever sporting with heaped multitudes of moving-and-static forms — bow.
To the magician, the pure, the hidden, the self-manifest; the subtle, the all-formed — to wondrous Śambhu — bow.
To all power — whose play destroys the Brahmā-Viṣṇu-arrayed world — wonder-working — bow.
To You, the fathomless Hara-ocean — whose powers are gained by those wandering only its shores — bow.
To the lovely hundred-petalled Śambhu-lotus, dwelling mid mud of the Māyā-made dense world, unsmeared, shining — bow.
Auspicious, pure, treasure, self-ornamented; dear, ultimate-real, highest — to You — bow.
Ever bound, ever sharing liberation's portion; difference-free — to gracious someone Śambhu — bow.
In these three worlds whose essence is mockery alone — to You alone, secondless, ever-bliss-seated — bow.
Essence of right-observance yet desirer of left-observance; of all observances, to observance-free Śarva — bow.
Whoever is worshipped, however, wherever — and whoever, whatever god he be — to that god, bow.
Served by liberation-seekers, remover of all burning; of spread-out chosen loveliness — to You, boon-giver — bow.
To You, husband-Lord of the ever-festival, whose three worlds brim with unbroken bliss-rasa — bow.
What enjoys You in pleasure-first knowables — to that terrible host of Your powers — bow.
Even sages cannot know Him — yet those whose gestures love connects embrace Him. To that someone Becoming — bow.
To the supreme-nectar sheath, the supreme-nectar heap; reachable beyond far and near — to Becoming — bow.
I praise Your mantra-formed, clear-cool, unprecedentedly joyful, supreme-nectar-juicy form.
On oneness-fame's great cloth, full of immortality-nectar — where, Lord, there is no wonder — I praise Your teaching.
Thunderbolt to all doubt, fire to all fortune, world's-end to all inauspiciousness — we bow the Māheśvara path.
Victory, god! Bow upon bow to You; this whole world rests on You; of worlds You are supreme Lord; I am come to You for refuge, the One supreme.
Of things, the two courses that go by being and non-being — leaping over them — to the third, the wondrous Śambhu — bow.
Among gods, seers, and men in this unfree triple world — free are Your dependents, O Free One.
Remembrance of Your body inlaid with the whole universe — the one medicine for world-pain; who have it sit happy.
Whose white umbrella is the self-lit moon, whose fly-whisk the heaven-river's stream — He alone is Supreme Lord.
Grant me, Lord, a glance — luminous, cool, one, pure as a moon-digit, carrying nectar.
Fallen from Your consciousness-bliss ocean — these knowings, these drops — why are they not nectar-sweet-beautiful to me, Lord?
In Your love-rasa, Lord, hearts unmelted — the heartless alone — such deserve contempt.
Whose heart has met the Lord's — he alone is the vessel of ruling goddesses' powers.
Flooder alike of all joys and sorrows — Your meditation-nectar-flood, like lowlands filling.
What would their look not be, happiness-provisions-full — who never part from You, more than self, Lord?
I roar, I dance — my wishes are fulfilled, for my Lord is won, utterly charming.
Where no other knowable for action, no other yoga for knowing — yet what if knowledge? Consciousness alone, world-filled-one, expands.
Suddenly fled from them — hard, endless sorrows — whose speech forever holds the Śiva-sound.
Is there another, higher person, distinct by remaining Yours? You alone, great Person, support of all persons without remainder.
Victorious, world-venerable, Your slaves, Lord — for whom this saṃsāra-ocean is a play-great-lake.
Let other miseries sit — for Your devotees, "You manifest Yourself" — by this alone they are shamed.
"Nothing is beyond me" — yet therein I am a reciter, by that oneness; as truth, You point the rosary somewhere.
From being must come supreme being, and beyond that, Lord — and You are other than being and non-being both; hence You are being-non-being-formed.
Purer-shining than thousand-sun-ray-rise — yet You, all-worlds-pervading, are not seen.
Conscious-formed in the inert world, knower even in the known; great in the measured — hence You are the highest.
Enough with other cries — this alone, before the Lord: I cry sharp, Lord, I am bewildered, even knowing thus.
Mind — though fickle you are — even so you are praised, since you worship the refuge of refuges, the world's teacher, Ambikā's husband.
Having crossed the ladder-steps of various gods, reached Śiva's feet — yet on the lowest ground I stand even now; wonder, I do not quit it.
Reveal Your own path, hide all world-ways thoroughly — while I am, Lord, quickly Your ever-risen servant.
Śiva Śiva Śambhu Śaṅkara — swift pity on the refuge-seekers' lover! Fortune is near for whoever remembers Your lotus-feet-pair.
Those seated on Your foot-lotus-throne, making the world to taste — they laugh at Vir iñc, office-stained, not-self-ruled.
Nothing appears apart from Your light-body; so You are always already gained, Lord — though far by nature.
Some taste Your foot-lotus-juice as stale-difference-conduct; others instantly taste it as flawless, body-whole, duality-free.
Lord, like lightning at dawn gleams my nectar-smeared — if it stayed steadier, You are worshipped duly — what else?
Is there anything, thing or non-thing, apart from this? With great discernment decided here: as You are, so be plain to me.
By Your will alone, Lord, I was made to step on Your own path — then why do I behave just like a man, knowing nothing fit for Your feet?
Some god of Yours blooms in their hearts, a lovely supreme state — by whose story-thunder-cātakas they are long gladdened.
For Your devotees, by some play in You, this love has grown fat — so that separation-ground talk and memory fruit in union-festival.
The word, grown by strange-rasa-sprinkling, though uttered "Śaṅkara" hundreds of times — enters even sideways hearts, ever-fresh in purpose.
Victorious are they on whose face-orbits the Śiva-sound ever revolves — which, moon-spread from nectar-source, trickles supreme nectar, sweet.
The fierce world as if finished; mind's impurity thinned to none — and yet not even the smallest knocking at Your city-door-bolt.
Of minds eager for Your ever-blooming face-lotus-belly-gaze — do something, Lord, just a little, so You flash as facing me.
What happiness here apart from non-difference-mind, what other glory? So why does this servant's mind, abandoning her, go the wrong way?
May I never for a moment be unfit for Your serfdom — unless constantly, reverently tasting non-difference-wine.
These people truly do not see Your body, dirtied by duality-sight — and yet, all-knowing refuge-lover, do You not hear MY cry?
Do You remember, Lord, any desired sense-pleasure I ever asked? Give instead, always, Your body-vision-nectar as the only wish.
Since by Your will alone I stepped on Your Śiva-path, Lord — hundreds of good omens rose for me; what else should I seek from You?
Where the sun sets with the moon and all — that unconquered Śiva-night shines, self-light-spread-lustrous.
Even won rule in three worlds, O king of gods, I count tasteless — lacking Your foot-touch-nectar-rasa.
Alas, Lord, strong is this self-bond, made of Your un-fame, fashioned by You alone — first ignored by me, it never loosens a bit.
Though worshipped by the great, O king of gods, You ever stay the one-worshipper-form — seen outside and in, You shine in the seers' bodies forever.
Joined in enjoyment by mere touch-contact of Your lotus-feet — bring me, Lord, by the neck into Your house.
Head hair dyed by Your foot-lotus-dust-redness — when shall I frantically begin to dance?
You my sole Lord — this alone I always ask: dwelling inside You, may I be silent; otherwise, wise.
Ah nectar-ocean master! Ah sweet three-eyed One! Ah tasty deformed-eyed One! — thus may I dance, shouting.
Eyes half-closed by Your foot-lotus-touch — may I expand, reeling drunk on Your devotion-liquor-madness.
May I dwell anywhere, O All-pervading, mind-mountain on earth, where that practice is — uninterrupted, great-rasa, made of Your prattle.
Where You stand with the Goddess, many-formed, from palace to gate-tower — in that city may I dwell.
May Your sun-rays rejoice, Lord, until my heart-lotus blooms — for Your worship.
Favor me, Lord, so that my mind, fallen ever at Your feet, tasting this and that — melts like wax, flows like...
Whether from joy bursting pot-lids, or sorrow — from outside or inside feeling, appear to me, Lord.
Outside too, inside too — may that ever-streaming, Your coolest foot-lotus-touch-nectar, be mine always.
Plunging inside Your touch-nectar-lake — may that pleasure beyond all pleasures be mine always.
Take what I offer — passion and the rest, Lord; make it nectar and eat it with devotees.
Ever-full on whole-world-food, happily seated — Master, cast Your grace-glance-moment on servants.
Eyes half-closed, chewing inner devotion-wonder — "bow to me, to Śiva" — may I worship even straw.
Though I have gained Your being — seeing the world as my self-blaze — may I be unparted by devotion-rasa-enjoyments.
Since nothing else is to be desired, Lord — to You, the secondless, fullness is fitting.
Where there is laughter, dancing, where passion-aversion are eaten, devotion-nectar drunk — may I reach that place.
May that unprecedented-joy-perfume of thought-flowers about You firm up in my mind — till bad-smell of bad-habit perishes.
Where is love among passions, and where is loving at Hari's lotus-feet — thus teach my contradiction-loving heart what is good, O Deathless.
Though wandering even through yogic states, though turned away from objects — may I be only heart-melted by Your-thought-liquor-madness.
In speech, mind-thoughts, body-gestures made by senses — everywhere, always, may bhakti-rasa go before me as leader.
While Your name "Śiva Śiva Śiva" is chanted endlessly, Lord — may I taste some great unrepeatable rasa.
In the vastness flashing as endless consciousness-self, where all dull paths are drunk up — may I roam Your worship, countless consciousness-made ramparts uncounted.
For standing in self-body, clearly shining, eternal — nothing else is of use; firm be this thought — but dust of Your pure feet, Lord.
Something flashes sometime in mind, touching Your feet — where this whole world melts — show it always, in the nectar-lake, Lord.
Even a moment parted from You, Lord — of me burning dense always — may I be the ground of Your gaze.
In saṃsāra whose essence is parting — by You, dear Lord, may I be ever unparted, though parted from the world.
Wherever I go by body, speech, mind — all that is You alone: may this ultimate truth stand ever full for me.
As You are construction-free, great-bliss-full — so may my praise-speech become, just fitting.
Seeing thing after thing as consisting of You, by Your possession — may I roam desireless, joy-filled.
May I see the whole world full of Your being, Lord — by that alone content; then do not toil.
May things shine for me always, melting into You alone like cloud-bits in sky, moving toward ever-purer courses.
May there blaze for me, from Your middle, some jewel of Being — its self-light-spread destroying the endless dark-series.
What stage do You not rule, what could there be that is not Your body? Tired — by effortlessness may I reach You everywhere.
May limb-embrace-enjoyment with You happen to me by mere will — this much gained, Lord, what have I not won?
Appear! We make no other prayers miserable — we languish, seeking only You.
Having come to even-taste in You, bliss-river — may my mind drop at once this difference-based great disaster.
"This is mine, not this" — on passion-aversion's firm-nailed root may the axe fall inside: the certainty of oneness-with-You-made.
May the thought-stain-line melt; may unbarredness blaze in heart; bliss-rasa-flooded be my consciousness-body, Lord.
Me, rolled in the passion-made world-egg — may devotion-thought-mother feed me with rasas, till, wing-grown, I am a bird.
May this mind of mine gain skill in tasting the essence of Your foot-thought-nectar-rasa — ending all object-poison-clinging-longing.
By devotion-sun-ray-touch, may this mind-jewel release far away passion-kindled fire-drops.
In that state may I praise You constantly, aloud — where even Hari, Hara's horse (?), Brahmā wait outside.
By devotion-madness-born frenzy may I see with faculties unmaimed: the whole world as Śiva, and all acts as worship-stuff.
My mind-boy, having taken Your-devotion-family-maiden, having borne aṇimā-etc. sons — may she, firm-rooted, harden the mine-thought.
The grace-drop stationed in the Lord, and devotion come as if to meet me — when will the pair, joined, take root in such a body?
Born of chewing His lordship, may some inner joy-juice rise; here always be supreme for me — knowledge-yoga's glories far off.
Like the worldly, let my thirst for objects swell — only seeing them as Your body, unconstructed.
In body-grounds and in mind, Lord, and in breath's course where difference has come — and in those consciousness-paths — by Yourself be plain to me, Thyself.
May these thrilled faculties fall into their own seats — never, Lord, even slightly, the daring of non-difference-rupture.
Light, soft, white-pure, cool — contemplating by possession-force a body — may I exceed those dealings of the all-thing-road.
May my self-body bloom as You; may worlds join my limbs; may all this duality-sport, even recalled, become untellable.
May there rise, looking at such Yours, a flood of supreme nectar — so my filling of non-duality's dread gorge happens.
If ever by the thinnest union-drops — may I turn from all world-pleasures; or shall I, fallen from both, be...?
Ever at Your lotus-feet, of me the best hamsa moving in the lake — above from root below, and from inside, may devotion's lotus-stalk bend up, unborn Lord.
May all things come under thought's scope and vision's footing for me; may vision-thought-light-nectar-essences blaze supreme.
Lord, in crashing hardships, as names bend down, may I be — fear gone only while limb-joined, exceeding-joy-mad.
The universe woven in Your self is shown outside by You alone — what stands firm-certain: may it now shine plain.
When will my mind, eager to taste new-rasa-moist union, rush past all else to Your touch?
You-loving, worship-wealthy — when shall I, the eager one, see You face to face?
When, by thick love made needless-minded, shall I burst all great bolts with a crash and reach You?
When, Lord, shall I subdue all gods — heart-seated in my own consciousness-essence — by devotion's power?
When will my vast devotion-bliss-rasa festival be — where even distinction gets a name from beholding-joy?
Having suddenly recognized the fearless, generous, full, causeless, self-hidden Lord — when shall I shame Your people?
When, Lord, that beloved-ness of Yours by which it would not be fitting for You to flee from me anywhere?
When shall I be bathed by the approving sight of all beings whose selves are Your worship?
Devotion, the highest ground of knowledge, the highest state of yoga — when will my begging for it be full?
Seizing suddenly, holding hard, joy-overwhelmed — when shall I proclaim Your foot-treasure to all?
All-around pure-You-light-spread — when shall I so shine that no Māyā-shadow-cave is in me?
Having made all circles my own, need-free — when shall I be, Lord, leader of Your devotee-host?
Lord, You are the unprecedented ground of world-prides — when shall I be greatly proud, filled with Your devotion-rasa?
Well-set in never-object-empty glory-embrace — when shall I lie like at cool lotus-feet?
Of worship-wealth grown rich on devotion-liquor — when shall I reach the far shore, when be apt?
Tears first, stumbling, wandering, choked crying — laughing-lit face: when shall I get Your touch-rasa?
Shaking off this beast-people-like conduct — when shall I, O Śambhu, taste the self-form fit for Your devotion?
Siddhis gained, all heat-fear melted — when shall I play, devoted to drinking Your devotion-rasa-medicine?
Lord, when shall that cry of mine rise in speech — at which Your form flashes before me at once?
Mind set on hugging Your tight-tight lotus-feet — when shall I see You, thing or non-thing, without effort?
Surely intolerable to You, sole world-Lord: Your Maheśvaras and other world-folk on one level.
Who always follow Your feet with love — wherever gone, they enjoy certain pleasures.
Where He is husband and death-ender, whence sickness? Where His fortune is, what other fortune?
By whose moment-pleasure the All is gained — for him all time fills with Your bliss.
Moon: Your bliss-rasa drop fallen to earth; sun: Your destroyer-heat's spread spark.
Offering to this third eye of Yours, Lord — sole mark of some unworldly greatness.
Seen by Him alone, one joys in Your vision-etc.; or whose joy somehow — by it You are seen.
Those You're pleased with, whose hearts You've won — dragging from Your city, they've made the outer inner.
Apart from You the whole world looks same-eyed — but its Īśvara is You alone, the Uneven-eyed.
Leave aside: without Your power there is no being at all — and those whose denials of You don't stand without You.
If mind stood in You alone, barriers in-outside gone — what else would be needed, Lord?
Others wander, Lord, in the self itself, ill-placed; others wander in the self itself, well-placed.
Even untasted Your devotion-nectar, unseen You — by mere conduct with You, beings perfect.
We are Your servants, Lord — so as You bear Yourself for three worlds, bear us too, fully.
Though seen in supreme-bliss-nectar, in the world-self — for touch-rasa with You I hunger exceedingly.
All sorrows even of worldlings — joined to Your ghee-self, become bearable.
With You — omniscient, omnipotent, consciousness-formed — somehow the world's show, though unreal, is fitting.
Breathed by You, qualities throb — even clod-like — dancing wind-tossed like cotton fluff.
If self-pride in qualities were not — then by what would the world's show of sole-selfness with You stand?
Venerable even the dissolved great ones, purified by Your anger-fire-touch.
With Your broad-light body standing plain — Lord, why do I spread in darkness on all sides?
You alone undivided, my nectar-nature — yet of mortal natures I alone am the seat.
Whose speech-ornament is the name "Maheśvara," whose head bears the bow-mark — he alone is powerful.
Since You are being and non-being — then effortlessly, by own tune, Lord, why is accomplishment not mine?
Śiva's slave, Śiva-selfed — what joy would he not reach? By whom even chief gods are sated with nectar-wine.
Between heart and navel, beings' bile-bodied — You devour, great fire, all moving-unmoving.
This world, or friends, or kin — nothing is mine at all; but when You are all this, who else is mine?
"Master, Maheśvara, You directly — all the world is You alone" — may the thing itself succeed; and begging even in that is mere begging.
Even world-overlordship here seems straw to Your devotee; what fruit has good karma, Lord, without Your remembrance?
Since nothing at all is apart from You, world-cause — Your play is wondrous, yet praise never sticks.
"I am Yours, worship-bound" — always, unceasing, even by own tune, and in dream — why am I not so?
Who are touched even slightly by Your lotus-foot-born fragrance-dust — for them all enjoyed things, gods-sought, become rest.
In heart no other, in word and deed wholly other, O Śambhu — yet grace or check from the truly real: one work only.
Fool am I, suffering-laden, aging-fearful, powerless — Yours am I: Śambhu, so arrange that, past sorrow's road, I mount the highest yoke fast.
Lying at Your ear-place, my cries, trifling — become like water-drops in bamboo-joints turning pearl.
What is not gained, alas, even by those — Lord — who even by deceit delight a moment in Your name?
Śambhu Śarva moon-crested Śiva, three-eyed rosary-bearer, fierce-skulled, trident-armed, ocean of pity, world-builder by fierce power, blue-throated — destroy ill-fortune fast, give supreme success.
What would there be where the Lord does not make? What would the knower Śaṅkara destroys be?
Though pains, age, death here are boon-givers most haughty, and approved sounds unstable — yet I long, ever-pleasure-hungering, to stand long tasting Your feet for life-drink.
O Lord skilled at destroying the bowed-down's pain, treasure of good, matted one — act now so that, living, I win unshakable attainments, Your-worship-bound.
Bow to delusion-great-darkness-destroyer whose sole work is that, to over-bright light moon-marked.
No helper is wanted at all, no hinderer is seen in Your vision — yet all is flooded by You alone: how is it even so that You do not see?
From things, senses, awareness-middle, ever self-born — may I see Him, world-veiled.
How could things come to be, and how reach Your path of vision, inlaid by what great nature-limb? Rising and rising, from land-water-grass on, You scatter nectar-floods of creation over all things.
Sated with Your form-nectar, thirst uprooted, drunk — they wander at will.
Not then, not always, not once — where no time-thought is: such is Your vision, neither eternal nor otherwise.
May my mind, risen to see You, gain this yoga-fruit always: to enter Your nectar-house by mere resolve, for Your worship.
The clear-minded great ones' pure play and words shine plainly, playfully.
Dwelling between Your feet, fearless — in those and those world-grounds may I worship the Lord, unbarred in act.
Dissolved in Your foot-lake, melted seeking, honey-drunk to excess — may I roam satisfied, at will.
Whose resolve to worship arose even from pretense — his presence is assured, fitting.
Lord, with one-taste mind seeking nothing else — the all-laying Lord, easy — may I drink to fullness: am I what?
By You denied: all where You're absent is to be left; where it's You, to be taken — this is the essence-extract.
The world-born worshipped as chief by being inside You — how, Lord, could non-being outside be worshipped, or by whom?
Noiseless, thought-free, undistracted, always — in agitation too, face to face: I see You alone everywhere, Three-eyed.
Reveal Your abode where You ever are with the Goddess; foot-dust-ranked servants — why do they look faithless?
Come to path's seeing yet fled — whence, Lord, to me Your servant? Never for a moment here are You not every being's sight-object.
When with oneness-nectar's pure unbroken stream will You flood me, Lord — bringing past difference the measurer, gaining self and body, joy?
From my understanding fenced off from yonder world, a grain of world-establishment — that I be worshipped by You.
Seeing every thing each moment, O form beyond measure — may I see You well, my own Lord.
Why doesn't mind haunt what limbs love, the desired thing for desire? If no nature is harmed and my supreme wish is filled...
Hundreds, they say, by Your power, with this very eye — even plough-walking — always see Your body ahead.
No thought rises unstained by Your will; always good or else — thus I roam as Yours on earth, feast of Your foot unstopped.
May insight rise well in Your deep sayings; then practiced power too, and unpausing worship-addiction.
In dealings too, always, may this sense-heap appear to me as Your limb — not self-warranted.
Mind roaming freely in its fields, unswerving — may I ever be worship-skilled toward You.
Lord, by Your will alone Your slave I was made — another's no power here — yet why never see Your face-moon?
The eager toward You who face You as counter-form — ah, what would befall them, what practice would fruit for them?
May things be as things by Your being for me; thus may nothing be otherwise, nothing but You.
May nothing-at-all be nothing, something-at-all be something to me; in all ways may You be worship-received.
In brief, Lord, hear my definition of pleasure and pain, as they stand for me: union with You, my husband-Lord, is pleasure; separation from You is pain.
Even the subtlest inward moment when You do not appear — wipe it out everywhere, Lord, and reveal Your own stainless form.
May living, dying, or anything else be mine — abiding, always worshipping You in Your world-full body at the time of undying consciousness-nectar.
"I am the Lord, I alone am formed, learned, fortunate — who else is parallel to me in the world?" Such pride shines — supremely — in those who love You.
By the awareness of things exactly as they stand, make me fit for worshipping Your feet — me, born of telling non-duality's nectar that swallows renown.
Meditated upon, then seen, then the Lord Himself is touched. May this worship-festival of Yours be always mine, by Your power.
Seeing things as they stand, and Your worship-festival — this pair grounds each other, expanding always among devotees.
Through every sense-door, constantly, may I drink the wine of Your worship-rasa in all-filled feeling-cups — and be mad.
Where not an atom is felt as other, and all expands self-shining — there, Lord, keep me standing, Your constant worshipper, in Your city.
Though You posted even me to slaves' quarters by Your own will — am I not fit by seeing, even by foot-massage?
At the moment of grace's descent You never deliberate, Lord, never — so what has come over You now, delaying the rite of Your self-revelation to me?
In each object shining outside, and inside joined with the Goddess, may I always behold You, world-full — worshipped by my own hands.
May I always mount the Master's palace-palace, unobstructed, by mere resolve — bliss-freed in the play of drinking supreme-nectar-wine.
Whatever wonder arises in all fair things by mere touch — by that the unwavering worship Your body.
Swelling all by self-shining, You touch the universe touching form; whatever swirls by its own juice — that is the swelling world.
Who sees this whole object-circle without construction as Your body, Lord — the world filled with his own self's side — for him, ever-happy, whence fear?
The kālakūṭa poison set in Your throat's corner is great nectar to me; even taken nectar would be Your body of poison to me, if difference prevails.
Graced with song-mouths lovely with prattling of You, may I be — my heart forever gone to what Your worship-loving prefers.
Alas, the Supreme's play cannot be counted — and so the nectar-full body He gave me, He does not let me drink as I will.
Entering You — fathomless, construction-free, non-dual, devourer of all things' meaning — O Umā's Lord, may I always worship and praise.
Before my own master, treasure of victory-fortune — may I taste for a moment the nectar of victory-proclamation.
Victory: one Rudra, one Śiva, great god, great Lord — Pārvatī's lover, Śarva, eldest of all gods.
Victory: moon-mark-eyed sole mark of the three-worlds-Lord; victory: poison-mark-throated, who drank the black poison for the worlds' pain.
Victory: whose self is the embodied three powers, hundred-spike-bright-handed; victory: whose lotus-feet are worshipped, wishes accomplished by mere will.
Victory: bearer of a body beyond worlds, streaming a hundred beauties; victory: single-braided, Ganges-thinned, ash-seized.
Victory: smeared with milk-ocean-spread moonlight shade; victory: snow-ornamented with jewel-light risen from the Lord's limb-contact.
Victory: refuge like the one undying cool-rayed digit; victory: consecrated by ever-Ganges and universal lordship.
Victory: whose lowest-limb-touch purifies cowherds; victory: fixed-present where intoxicated devotees gather.
Victory: who dupes the childish, showing a hot place of His own will; victory: fit vessel for Gauri-embrace-fortune.
Victory: greedy for love-gifts wet with devotion-rasa; victory: pleased by the speech-dance of devotees drunk with devotion.
Victory: whose rise-and-fall is the power of Brahmā-and-first-gods; victory: whose command world-lord-rows bear on heads.
Victory: whose manifest glory is His seal set on all worlds; victory: great Lord of all, down to giving the very self.
Victory: secondless at the creation-wish moment; victory: with sole Goddess-helper bearing lordship's burden.
Victory: who seized all three worlds in one stride; victory: unbroken Lord-sound sung from childhood.
Victory: innately high, needing no pity and the rest; victory: Bhairava before whom great Death is made.
Victory: unopposed in fierce world-ending acts; victory: hundredfold-good-named recitation-following.
Victory: nectar-mine-ocean poured out in play; victory: whose instant anger dries the world-ending in a flash.
Victory: sole lamp of beings blind in delusion-darkness; victory: wakeful supreme Person while the sleeping world...
Victory: life-of-life humming inside the body-mountain cave; victory: best rasa sporting in good minds' sky.
Victory: mountain-lord born of high gold-ore; victory: moon rising as calamity-portent over the wicked.
Victory: hard to reach by austerity-tormented sages and gods; victory: seen by the world of devotion-madmen mounted on every state.
Victory: who leafed His dependents spreading His own wealth; victory: whose sole purpose is fondling surrendered people.
Victory: sole performer of creating-staying-destroying; victory: festival of the play-lotus blooming in drunken devotion.
Victory, worthy of victory! Victory, conqueror of birth, aging, dying! Victory, eldest of worlds... victory, victory... O three-eyed One.
Stain-washing books exist, and their crossers too — yogins, scholars stand healthy — but devotees alone, in truth.
Māyā-time-limit-passion and the rest as food, fully fed — devotees stroll happy, Lord, on the world's shore.
Laughing or crying, they babble You aloud — devotees, whose praise-word offerings are ornaments apart.
Not detached, not master, not liberation-desiring is Your worshipper — but drunk with soaring devotion-liquor-rasa.
Who worships by drawing the outer inside the heart alone — to him, in devotion-nectar floods, I bow.
Between dharma and adharma acts, knowledges, pleasure and pain selves — devotees taste SOMETHING — ah!
Blind ones, lepers even — they shine, supreme, ornamented by blazing devotion to You.
Gleaners, winnowers, enemies' shadows even — yet by devotion's heat they rule even the king of kings.
Though rolling in nectar-wet devotion, yet wanting to climb — some worship You with mind alone, standing all around.
To be guarded, grown, honored, Lord — this great wealth of devotion that ends bad rebirths.
Lord, though Your devotees love You — abandoning jealousy toward Her, may She always be pleased, the Mistress.
Your future being first; when devotion's occasion comes and the milk-ocean is churned — curd-greed is killed.
Is this not attainment beyond compare — ever-growing devotion to Śambhu, always new? What happiness does it not stream?
Sunk in my dirty mind, Your devotion gem-creeper — alas — does not spread its own splendor's unfoldings.
Devotion to the Lord of three worlds IS supreme attainment — but lacking supernormal powers, is it not full? — that is my worry.
Outside and in, the fragrance of Your praise-blossoms' opening perfumes even hostile ascetics dwelling near.
By no account is there any light; the whole world fast asleep — yet at Your Śivarātri post, devotees always worship You.

Let goodness expand in true worship of gracious Śiva; let Śaṅkara-foot-dust heaps sport on the crown — to cut even passion-memories, let darkness swell, or the triple world dissolve in Your self-loss.

The world-road is long; limbs burnt by harsh diseases; pleasures unenjoyed; happiness never long — thus I have become useless, moon-crest-foot-pressed, wholly Yours — so make me, quickly, long-and-rich in great fortune, as Your devotee.
Nothing blocks folk, nothing blocks devotees from Your veiling.
Though reached by method-ladders, crowded with attributes — to devotees the self appears at once, pure.
Laughing victors, laughing conquered — drunk on His devotion-nectar, whoever they are, Lord.
May I never dry up, never seek release — full of His devotion-rasa, best-liked, attained.
As unknown before was this devotion-rasa of Yours to me — so, Lord, may that same one grow.
Truly, Lord, I have no other prayer-course — only may such immersion-possession by devotion be mine always.
Drunk on devotion I may rage, repent, leap, shout "Śiva" — enough.
In crisis or at peace, weeping or laughing, deep or distracted — may I be, Lord, by devotion.
For devotees nothing to be known, inside You or out — where consciousness-natured You stand thought-free.
Devotees rejoice even at abusers — pierced within, bristling with sharp horripilation, as if by nectar-drops.
Even pain-feeling ripens to enjoyment for devotees, whose all-awareness, moon-wet, is moonlight-made.
Wherever held, devotees — inside and out — unfeigned, Your body-touch-taste-joy the same.
In worship of Your devotion, duality's double-refuge meanness — tasting the clear nectar-body, some dissolve it.
Erring are pilgrim-eyes, divided — for division is just erring; but matchless, strifeless Being shines for devotees.
Mind ripened past honor, contempt, love and the rest into stainlessness — how could its bearer be world-mannered?
Passion-aversion-darkness conquered by devotion-light — who are the knowledge-rich before them?
Whose rite is devotion-nectar-drink-and-bath — high joy from beginning through end.
Praised, sought, worshipped — for that alone devotees' world-life is praiseworthy.
Liberation's name is but Your ripe devotion — mounted on its first stage, we are near-free.
May pain's coming be great for me, devotion-filled self — never turned from You, be even pleasure-line.
You are pleased by devotion; devotion, You pleased — this mutual dependence is fitting, as You alone know.
With form or formless, inside or out — to devotion-selves, always nectar, Lord.
In this very world, for Your devotees, another world-stand exists — fruit of joy-showing.
Devotion hidden, devotion supreme, devotion to the world-great Lord — devotion, ah, something in You, Śiva.
Devotion, devotion, supreme devotion — I cry loud: let fierce devotion be mine supreme.
Since I am the birth-ground of all beauties — stuck to You, jewel or straw becomes priceless.
From knower and from knowable, on whose knowing-road there is no parting from You — they win, Your devotees, ever fearless.
Embraced in saṃsāra's hall by some, You — Lord, by others self-tormenting unreined.
With Śivā who eats, decks, celebrates the world, festival-hurried — hug tight, Śiva, I bow.
Peerless overlordship wins, world-Lord, being subject-free — and so does Your otherness, by which this world shines as it does not.
Ah, this wins — sweet, this festival of worship — since tears give nectar-taste amply.
All acts with His worship vanguard are successes; devotees made of Him are themselves successes.
In all beings, all states, at once, all-formed — worshipping You unceasing, they are my gods.
Meditation-perfected touch-festival of You — thus famed as worship-rule — be mine always.
Equanimity-essence equinox-moment of devotees is always — ever-worshipping with Your being-rasa-nectar.
Whose beginning and end are not, nor time-order — that deed is Yours, and its doers resort only to You.
Brahmā and the rest are fortunate, lords — in whose dream, even delusion, stands Your worship-festival.
Chanting, offering, bathing, meditating — and not only: ah, devotees' worshipping You — whenever, whatever, however much.
Tasting Your worship-nectar-joy, enjoying — to Indra and the rest, to Brahmā-chiefs: is anyone equal?
World-shaking, one-cause festival — what is got thereby, only devotees know who get it.
Standing in Your abode, consciousness-formed, with body-speech-mind acts of all 36 principles — I always worship You, Lord.
Of me, enjoying union with Your worship — may all time pass, even endless: this I pray.
Greedy for Your worship-enjoyment-nectar — may it grow daily for me and fruit always.
In Your ocean, nectar-one-rasa-full, worshipping You, great self, may I always sit.
Mind offered as sweet in Your rite — knots ever cut simply.
Having taken stand on objects — these sense-courses of devotees — send them for Your worship-nectar-wine.
Agitated by devotion-heat, self-mastered — what else could liberate but drowning in worship of You?
Perpetual foot-worship-nectar-drinking festival — may it be my sole grace-getting cause, Lord.
Experiencing, Lord, moment by moment — Your worship-nectar-drinking-madness-joy-great-joy.
Seen is the point of devotees' great worship-undertaking: that they taste impossible joy then.
Till Your worship-nectar-taste-festival is got, I count no drop of fortune's happiness tasted.
Without sense-seeking strain, Your abode's abiding is born in devotees — no getting needed, only madness with worship.
Nothing ungettable for devotees, nothing hard — they only roam, mad with worship.
Ah, the devotees' heart-heavy worship-rule: praised, unmarked by begging.
What beauty is not, what joy not, what fortune not, what liberation not — this Mahādeva, since He is worshipped.
In all-empty... may this body be nourished as Your worship-thing, always devoted.
Dependent on Your foot-worship-enjoyment — may I, O world-Lord, be the one self-willed in movement.
To quench vision-touch-thirst for You — arises the cool, sweet great lake of Your worship.
As You alone are the world's worship-enjoyment-vessel — so, Lord, is the devotee a vessel of worship-enjoyment.
Victor, Your festival — even the 36 agitated by it — great day.
Bow to those whose worship-things are themselves worshipped, by devotion-nectar-water.
At worship's start, meditating mantra-placed His selfhood — devotees rest in supreme self, nowhere roaming.
Kingdoms blooming, world shared out in nectar-wine by festival-goers.
Whose moment-drink is worship-nectar — are they gods, freed, or whatever people?
The world's dignity as worship-gear is theirs — ah, something of devotees, and just lightness!
From worship-made eye-throw agitation, nectar-rising for devotees — as from the gods' milk-ocean churning.
Some take worship as the wish-cow; others, inward-turned, milk the nectar-stream.
Even eye-throws, world-approved, bring something within — may the festival grow.
By devotion-agitation, worship in self-become-Him — wonder: poverty's top fruit is lowliness' fruit.
For some, rite is upacāra-step to His feet; for devotees, non-duality-bliss-spread.
Spread by unbound mad devotion to the formless-seeming, it gains some foothold in You.
Taste-stunned mind; He alone as worship's vessel, they say.
Full, pure, steady, devoted means be mine for His worship, Lord.
In the whole worship-treasure, what fortune of the organ-host blooms?
This prettiness is Yours alone, Lord: though Lord of all, worshipped by servants — and found.
Rise from formed or formless, being or non-being — may my festival rise.
With lust, anger, pride made offering, who always worship — bow to them; of them I am pleased, in truth.
Victor, Your festival of devotees' supreme rule — though made with straw, yet furnished with jewels.
Finding You inside the world, they get inside You — never far are Your devotees.
He here, She everywhere, pregnant with the order of all things, supreme — but at the ultimate step, no division of Her nor of the triple world.
The ungrateful know not the auspicious, though proud; all things, though effort-favored — but this mind, though risen, does not perceive the self-form here; ah, alas, I am destroyed.
Who has gained dwelling in the self made of You, Your feet worshipped with full wealth — needing neither food nor covering ever: to him I bow.
Ever dwelling in Your body-abode yet inwardly supreme-burning, this world — by Your will make me here, of worship-joy-nature.
Spontaneously risen, touching Your lotus-feet pair, drinking the worship-nectar — mind intent, may I be, in gathering my aims, with mere touch-happiness as world-tour.
In the whole field of dealings, plainly, while You throb inside, Lord — coming and going ever, may my things shine always.
Ever in Your city, or parted and roaming — may I be, by You: never even a moment's defeat for me, where I am become of You.
Filled all round with cool nectar-floods streaming from Your limbs — in the wealth of worshipping You here, Your devotees move in saṃsāra's middle.
In the cool shade of the great-mantra tree, in Your great forest, in my own self always, Lord, may I dwell as Your worshipper.
As everything living mirrors You, mirror-formed — so before me, Lord, come forth graced with three eyes and trident.
From pride-offering, love-held devotion-built — pleased, when will You be everywhere my eyes' ground?
Dwelling in the nectar-ocean middle, mind drowned in Your worship-rite alone — may I do all people's business, tasting everything everywhere.
Your thing here, Your truth — who is fit to disclose the matter? This same name-form-sport-unequalled of Yours takes away — since You are Hara, the Taker.
For peace, no hankering for pleasure at all, among those drunk with devotion amassed — nor even begging the fruit of seeking liberation remembered before the heart-thief.
Waking or other state, or any beyond, while slightly steady — for the devotee-people, all is Your festival in the ever-present mind.
Mind's eye-wheel courses, everywhere loosened yet still — reaching You, of firm-long awareness: Lord, how, by devotion-wealth's heat?
Nothing unmade, no unpleasure made — yet all suffers and divides: bow to the wonder-abode.
Of me whose thought-stain is washed bright by hard-denier nectar-filling flood, whose unconquered-doubt-foe is crushed — may Your sight be unbroken.
Enter plainly, then I shall enter You — always, Lord, for I am Yours: with violent speed may I worship Your body face to face.
In You no one's is praise-power — yet it exists since You are so beautiful; my constant prayer again is this: that I behold You, Lord, unwearied.
Beyond prayer-grounds, strange-fruit-giver — victorious, unprecedented in story, Śiva the true wish-tree.
Since from the One container all is got through the self, from You — yet my own self does not join You, the highest, Her.
The self, knowledge-action-formed consciousness-body, is in every way the Lord alone — but would there even be a body among all these things, or what else?
By unequalled fruit, stealing pain — melt into His sight-natured form; may my going be His-formed.
When will foot-thought-jewel-creeper-fruition, amazing the perfected, befall me, from You?
When, Lord, shall I fully see Your pure face-orb, from which streams unprecedented nectar-flood, which drowns the whole world?
Your form, risen at mere meditation — when, Lord, will it ever fill with supreme-nectar floods my far gaps named non-duality-liberation?
By touch of Your peerless rasa, unroaming abandoned — not even now is my mind, Lord: when will it be? Let it be soon.
Not dry-bitter things only — bring on all, always, gained by offering to You; let even opposites befall me.
Lord, may Your pure rays come face to face, as long as body-mind-heat-dark is wiped out.
God, be gracious till my path-blockers, truth-stealing, sense-thieves are tamed.
With Your devotion-nectar-essence fill my mind fast, Lord — till these are carried off, drowned: all sapless habits.
In liberation-state, where is devotion to You — how could it shine even for the mortal-natured? So set me, Unborn, on a fitting attainment-ground.
Greedy for a siddhi-drop's gain, don't settle proud me — thin is liberation beside Your devotion-face's sprouting aṇimā-wings.
May the Lord be pleased with me, His slave — I ask only this, since the three-worlds Giver exceeds my sight.
In mind full of Your body-mindfulness-nectar-rasa, may Your lotus-feet-pair bloom in mine, ever dripping honey, supramundane.
I have a Lord, a father — Tryambaka — and a mother, Bhavānī; no second exists for me here — thus most-fulfilled may I roam.
Bow to the three-worlds' Lord, ash-white, three-eyed, trident-bearing, snake-threaded, moon-crested.
I praise, self-forgetting, white-robed in bite-torn cloth, dancing to the tune of the skull-garland.
Bow to those whose god is Hara, whose acts are Hara-fit, whose lives lean wholly to Hara — the fortunate abodes.
Your play, behind lordship — and this too, as wished-fulfilled in gifts, by self I reach the supreme means.
In Your world-venerated abode, in this play — how great would my bliss-birth be?
How could He not be fortunate — Hara, Gauri's beloved? And how could Hara not be Gauri's supreme beloved?
Whose meditation-nectar is undying, self-rooted, ever-fresh consciousness-creepers, like some tree of being.
At devotion-itch's showing, Lord's pillar-firmness arises — by it the world, great festival, is won.
Ever to creation-sport, ever seated in staying-pleasure, ever world-eating-sated — to the husband, bow.
Nowhere gone, nothing left — who see Your abode as to-be here, fortunate: bow to them.
For the devotion-fortuned, what else is begged; for the devotion-poor, what else is begged?
Where pains turn pleasures, poison turns nectar, saṃsāra turns liberation — that path is Śiva.
At root, middle, end, no suffering for Your people — yet we sink, Lord: tell why.
Light is worth begging even by others, beginners in knowledge-yoga — You, Lord of devotees, are like the light of the free.
Devotees have no prayers, no remembrance of You the self — yet this "Śiva" of theirs, something, on the lip.
Who lights all appearances, wrapped in vimarśa — "I am this": I praise Your action-power, Lord.
All beings, from Brahmā to Viṣṇu, being devoured — so I bow, God, to the world as Your-formed.
All beyond Me is false, by relation to destruction — thus engaged, Lord, by Your destruction-play alone.
Meditated, Your form stands present for devotion-rich — unconquered by unthinkable-wonder-makers.
By Your devotion-wine-taste nerves' thrill, night-heroes dance, roused by vetālas.
The praise begun with this limb of mine — by it may all this time be firmly unending.

He alone — Śiva, possessing spanda, self-established — who makes the inner face taste.
